summary: The Agbami Medical and Engineering Professionals Scholarship was started in 2009 by Star Deep Water Petroleum (a Chevron company) and its Agbami field partners. It gives a yearly grant to full-time undergraduates studying Medicine and Surgery, Dentistry, Pharmacy or Engineering at Nigerian universities; over 16,000 students have benefited. Winners apply with clean, matching documents and score well in a computer-based qualifying test.
lookfor: Enrolment in Medicine and Surgery, Dentistry, Pharmacy or Engineering, full time, at an accredited Nigerian university
The right year of study for that round (100/200 level in 2019; 200 level in the 2021/22 round)
Complete documents, including department verification and consistent names
Performance in the computer-based qualifying test (past rounds: verbal, numerical and abstract reasoning plus current affairs, as reported)
cycle: No new round has been confirmed since the 2021/22 campaign (closed 17 Jan 2022). Past rounds opened at different times of year (e.g. Oct-Nov in 2015 and 2019, around Dec-Jan in 2021/22), so prepare now and watch Chevron Nigeria and major newspapers - check the current guidance.

eligibility.q: Are you a Nigerian studying full time at an accredited Nigerian university?
eligibility.no: Only full-time students at Nigerian universities were eligible.

eligibility.q: Is your course Medicine and Surgery, Dentistry, Pharmacy or Engineering?
eligibility.no: Other courses were not eligible. Try NNPC/TotalEnergies NMSS or NLNG, which cover more fields.

eligibility.q: Are you in the year of study the current advert names (recently 200 level; 100 or 200 level in 2019)?
eligibility.no: Check the current guidance. If you are too early or too late, apply to NLNG (first-years) or NMSS (100/200 level).

eligibility.q: Do you hold no other STAR-sponsored scholarship?
eligibility.no: Past rules said awardees cannot hold other STAR-sponsored scholarships.

eligibility.q: Are your O'Level and JAMB results available with your admission letter?
eligibility.no: Get printed copies from WAEC/NECO and the JAMB portal before applying.

steps.title: Check whether a round is actually open
steps.why: Agbami rounds are irregular and many sites recycle old adverts or sell fake forms. Checking first protects you.
do: Search for 'Agbami scholarship' news from Chevron Nigeria or major newspapers (Vanguard, Punch, BusinessDay) dated this year.
Find the official application portal named in the advert. Past portals were run by appointed consultants and changed between rounds.
If no current advert exists, keep preparing using the steps below and check monthly.
Write your backups: NNPC/TotalEnergies NMSS, NLNG, state scholarships.
tips: Real adverts name Star Deep Water Petroleum Limited and the Agbami parties.
avoid: Paying for 'Agbami application forms' or 'past questions' on blogs or WhatsApp.
check: I know whether a round is open, and I have backups.

steps.title: Understand how Agbami selects
steps.why: There is no essay. Your documents get you to the test, and the test decides.
do: Note past stages: online application, department verification, computer-based qualifying test at centres nationwide, award.
Read a past advert to see the document list and warnings.
Plan most of your preparation time for aptitude practice.
tips: Test invitations came by email and SMS - keep both active.
avoid: Assuming a high CGPA alone wins.
check: I know the stages and where my effort goes.

steps.title: Set up email, phone and a document folder
steps.why: Activation links and test invitations come by email and SMS.
do: Use a personal email you check daily and your own phone number.
Create a folder named 'Agbami' on your phone and laptop.
Set a monthly reminder to check for a new advert.
tips: Add any official portal address to your contacts so mails avoid spam.
avoid: Using a shared or parent's email.
check: I have a working email, phone and folder.

steps.title: Fix name mismatches first
steps.why: Past adverts said names must match on all documents, or you must provide a sworn affidavit.
do: Compare names on WAEC/NECO, JAMB result, admission letter, birth certificate and school ID.
If any differ, swear an affidavit at a High Court registry.
Scan the affidavit.
tips: Do this before anything else - courts can be slow.
avoid: Hoping no one notices a different spelling.
check: My names match or I have an affidavit.

steps.title: Gather and scan all required documents
steps.why: An incomplete upload is not shortlisted.
do: Get: school ID card, admission letter, O'Level result, JAMB result, birth certificate and LGA identification letter (from your Local Government secretariat).
Take a passport photo on a white background, less than three months old.
Resize the photo to the size the advert asks (2019: 450 x 450 pixels, under 200 KB) using a free photo editor.
Scan every document clearly and name files sensibly.
tips: Keep originals together - you may need them at the test centre.
avoid: Photos that are too large, dark or old.
check: Every document is scanned and the photo meets the size rule.

steps.title: Arrange department (HOD) verification
steps.why: In past rounds the application was verified by your Head of Department before final processing.
do: Tell your HOD or course adviser you are applying.
Ask how verification works in your department and how long it takes.
When you submit, follow up so the HOD verifies before the deadline.
tips: Give the department office a printed summary of what to verify.
avoid: Submitting on the last day when the HOD cannot respond in time.
check: My HOD knows and is ready to verify.

steps.title: Prepare a details sheet (no essay required)
steps.why: Past forms had no essay, but asked many personal and academic details. A sheet prevents mistakes.
do: Write your full names, date of birth, state and LGA, university, faculty, course, level and matriculation number.
Add your O'Level and JAMB details.
Keep it beside you while filling the form.
tips: Copy names exactly as on your admission letter.
check: My details sheet matches my documents.

steps.title: Register on the official portal and fill the form
steps.why: Only one complete application per person is accepted.
do: Open the portal named in the current official advert and register.
Activate your account from the email link.
Fill personal and educational information from your details sheet.
Upload each document in the right place and preview it.
tips: Use a laptop with stable internet.
avoid: Creating a second account - multiple applications were disqualified.

steps.title: Check, submit and keep proof
steps.why: Errors in uploads were a common reason for rejection.
do: Re-check every uploaded document opens and is correct.
Submit at least a week before the deadline.
Screenshot the confirmation and save emails.
tips: Ask a friend to double-check your scans.
avoid: Submitting at midnight on the closing day.
check: I have saved proof of submission.

steps.title: Prepare for the qualifying test
steps.why: The computer-based test at centres nationwide is the main filter.
do: Practise verbal reasoning (comprehension, vocabulary) daily.
Practise numerical reasoning (percentages, ratios, data tables) with a timer.
Practise abstract reasoning (shapes and patterns).
Read Nigerian current affairs, especially health and energy news.
tips: Practise on a computer to get used to the screen and timer.
avoid: Buying 'Agbami past questions' from unknown sellers.
check: I have done at least five timed practice sets.

steps.title: Attend the test
steps.why: Missing the test or arriving without ID ends your application.
do: Read the invitation email or SMS carefully for date, time and centre.
Plan transport to arrive at least an hour early.
Bring your invitation, school ID and any original documents requested.
Follow the centre's rules - no phones on the desk.
tips: Visit the centre a day before if it is far away.
check: I know my centre and have my ID packed.

steps.title: Accept the award and keep it
steps.why: The grant continues yearly only if you remain in good standing.
do: Follow the award email to submit any extra documents and bank details through the official process only.
Keep copies of every award letter.
Maintain your grades and submit results when asked.
avoid: Sharing bank details outside the official process.
check: I have accepted the award in writing.

videos.why: Past applicants' walk-throughs; check the date of any video against the current advert.

videos.t: YouTube search: aptitude test practice Nigeria

faq.q: Is the Agbami scholarship open now?
faq.a: No new round was confirmed when checked (October 2026); the last public campaign closed in January 2022. Watch Chevron Nigeria and major newspapers.

It is a yearly grant until graduation. Past reports said it was higher for medical students than for engineering students - check the current advert.
No. Never pay for forms or past questions.

faq.q: What can I apply for meanwhile?
faq.a: NNPC/TotalEnergies NMSS (100/200 level), NLNG (first-years) and your state scholarship board.
